usageNotes: Use this to perform a clean reboot of a running QEMU VM — it shuts the guest down gracefully then starts it again, which also applies any pending configuration changes (e.g. CPU/memory adjustments that require a restart). The call is asynchronous and returns a UPID string; poll the task status endpoint to confirm completion. The VM must be in a running state and the caller needs VM.PowerMgmt on /vms/{vmid}.

examples.summary: Reboot VM 101 on node pve1 with a 60-second shutdown timeout

destructiveReason: The VM's running services are interrupted during the shutdown-and-start cycle, causing a brief outage for any workloads hosted on the guest.
tips: Omitting 'timeout' lets Proxmox use its default shutdown wait; set an explicit value if the guest is known to be slow to shut down.
This endpoint applies pending hardware changes (CPU sockets, RAM, etc.) that a simple reset would not — prefer it over a stop+start sequence for config rollouts.
The returned UPID can be passed to GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to watch progress.
If the guest OS ignores ACPI shutdown signals (e.g. no guest agent, misconfigured), the shutdown may hang until the timeout expires and Proxmox force-stops the VM.
